matters.title: Resolution to Approve a Purchase Order to Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. for Pacific Tek Water Gate Valve Exercising Equipment (North Carolina Sheriffs Association - $87,821.00)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Purchase Order to Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. for Pacific Tek Water Gate Valve Exercising Equipment (North Carolina Sheriffs Association - $87,821.00) 
..Memorandum
The attached resolution approves the purchase of Pacific Tek Water Gate Valve Exercising Equipment from Infrastructure Solutions Group for a total of $87,821.00 through the North Carolina Sheriffs Association (NCSA) cooperative purchasing program (NCSA# 24-08-0421) for use by the Public Works Unit of the Public Services Area. 

Gate valve exercising equipment is used to operate water valves located on water main lines that supply the community with water. These valves are used to isolate portions of the water distribution system when necessary for new construction or emergency repairs. The new equipment includes specialized programming that senses the torque necessary to turn the valves and executes automated exercising programs until the valve operates as it should. This data is then logged for further analysis by staff. It also includes a vacuum unit that will be used to remove debris from valve boxes and gate wells saving follow up trips with additional equipment to clean out debris for access. The equipment currently used for this process is at the end of its useful life and must be replaced.
 
Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. was awarded contract #24-08-0421 by the North Carolina Sheriffs Association cooperative purchasing program for heavy equipment. Fredrickson Supply of Grand Rapids, MI, will prep, deliver and provide future service for the equipment.

Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination ordinances.

Budget/Fiscal Impact:  Adequate funding for the purchase of this equipment is available in the FY24 Water Supply System Operations and Maintenance budget.
..Staff
Prepared by:	       Paul Matthews, Public Works Manager 
Reviewed by:	       Brian Steglitz, Public Services Area Administrator 
Approved by:        Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, Public Works needs to purchase replacement water gate valve exercising equipment; 

Whereas, Competitive bids were received by the North Carolina Sheriffs Association (NCSA) cooperative purchasing program and Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. was awarded contract# 24-08-0421 for gate valve exercising equipment;

Whereas, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination Ordinances; and
Whereas, Adequate funds for this purchase are available in the approved FY2024 Water Supply System Operations and Maintenance budget. 

RESOLVED, That City Council approve the issuance of a purchase order to Infrastructure Solutions Group, Inc. for gate valve turning equipment in the amount of $87,821.00;

RESOLVED, That funds for the purchase of this equipment comes from the Water Supply System Operations and Maintenance budget;

RESOLVED, That the amount herein is without regard to fiscal year; and 

RESOLVED, That the City Administrator be authorized to take the necessary actions to implement this resolution.

matters.title: Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order to Idexx for Bacteriological Testing Media and Associated Supplies  ($36,000.00)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order to Idexx for Bacteriological Testing Media and Associated Supplies  ($36,000.00)
..Memorandum
Attached for your review and approval is a resolution to authorize the purchase of bacteriological media and associated supplies for the Water Treatment Services Unit's Environmental Services Laboratory in the amount of $36,000.00. The Environmental Services Laboratory uses bacteriological media and associated sampling supplies to perform analysis of microorganisms in the drinking water, stormwater, and wastewater for compliance with state and federal regulations.

The use of Idexx bacteriological media is necessary for these tests as it is a proprietary product that does not cause testing interferences as observed with other similar-use projects made to detect total coliforms and E. coli in water. Our drinking water laboratory certification identifies the Idexx product as the only product we can use to run this analysis and Idexx is the only seller of their products. Idexx complies with the requirements of the Non-discrimination and living wage. 

It is recommended that City Council award a purchase order to Idexx to provide the Environmental Services Laboratory bacteriological testing media and associated supplies. It is also recommended that the purchasing agreement may be renewed for three (3) additional one (1) year periods, provided that by 90 days prior to end of the contract both parties agree to an extension at no more than 3% increase in cost if the vendor is agreeable and if the city deems it to be in its best interest. 

Budget/Fiscal Impact: Funds for this purchase are available in the approved FY25 Water Supply System Fund, Sewage Disposal fund, and Stormwater Fund Operating and Maintenance Budgets. Future contract years are subject to City Council's annual budget approval. City Charter language requires sole source procurement over $25,000.00 receive City Council approval.
..Staff
Prepared by:	LJ Melrose, Environmental Laboratory Supervisor
Reviewed by:	Sue McCormick, Interim Public Services Area Administrator 
Approved by:	Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, The City's Environmental Services Laboratory uses bacteriological media and related supplies to conduct water quality testing for compliance with State and Federal Regulations;

Whereas, The City's laboratory certification by the State of Michigan identifies Idexx as the proprietary bacteriological media to use in tests for detection of microorganisms;  

Whereas, Funding for this purchase is available in the approved FY25 Water Supply System and Sewage Disposal System Fund budgets;

Whereas, City Charter language requires sole source procurement over $25,000.00 receive City Council approval; and

Whereas, Idexx complies with the requirements of the Non-discrimination and Living Wage; 

RESOLVED, That City Council approve the issuance of a purchase order to Idexx Laboratories for the purchase of bacteriological media and related supplies in an amount not to exceed $36,000.00 in FY25;

RESOLVED, That subject to the availability of funding, the City Administrator is authorized to and directed to renew the purchase order for up to three one-year periods, not to exceed $36,000.00 per year including the 3% price escalation; and

RESOVLED, that the City Administrator be authorized to take all necessary actions to implement this resolution.

..Title
Resolution to Authorize A Sole Source Purchase Order with Jack Doheny Companies Inc. for the Purchase of Parts and Service for Water, Sanitary and Storm Sewer Equipment (Not to Exceed $190,000.00 Annually)
..Memorandum
The proposed resolution authorizes the purchase of truck and equipment replacement parts, related accessories, and service in amount not to exceed $190,000.00 per year from Jack Doheny Companies Inc. of Northville, MI for FY25 and FY26, subject to the availability of funding FY26.

Jack Doheny Companies Inc. is the sole Michigan supplier of sales, parts, and repairs for Vactor Manufacturing Inc., including their Vactor, Ramjet and Guzzler product lines. The advantages of sole source supply includes reduced inventory requirements and the familiarity that mechanics have to diagnose and repair equipment in a timely manner.

The City's four vacuum trucks are all Vactor trucks. The requested amount for each fiscal year for parts and repairs is based on Fleet Service's regular maintenance history for these vehicles. 

The purchase order will be split between Public Works for parts and repairs related to the truck mounted equipment such as sewer line cameras, cleaning jets and nozzles, and Fleet Services, for parts and repairs to the actual vacuum truck. Public Works will utilize up to $100,000.00 annually and Fleet Services will utilize up to $90,000.00 annually.

Budget/Fiscal Impact:  Adequate funding for the purchase of truck and equipment parts and services is available in the approved FY25 Fleet Services Operations and Maintenance Budget, Water Supply System, Sewage Disposal System and Stormwater System Operations and Maintenace Budgets. Award of the FY26 purchase order would be subject to the availability of funds in these budgets.

Jack Doheny Companies Inc. complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination Ordinances.

Matthew J. Kulhanek, Fleet and Facilities Unit Manager
Reviewed by:		John Fournier, Deputy City Administrator
Approved by:  	Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, Jack Doheny Companies Inc. is the sole Michigan supplier of sales, parts and repairs of the Vactor Manufacturing Inc. including their Vactor, Ramjet and Guzzler product lines;

Whereas, Jack Doheny Companies Inc. complies with the City's conflict of interest and non-discrimination ordinances; and 

Whereas, Adequate funding for the purchase order is available in the approved FY2025 Fleet Services, Water Supply System, Sewage Disposal System and Stormwater System Operations and Maintenance Budgets and will be available in subsequent annual budgets if approved by Council;

RESOLVED, That City Council approves sole source purchase orders to Jack Doheny Companies Inc. in an amount not to exceed $190,000.00 in FY2025 and not to exceed $190,000.00 for FY2026 subject to the availability of funding in FY2026; and

..Title
Resolution to Approve a Two (2) Year Construction Contract with Watertap, Inc. for Watermain Line Stops and Insertable Valves (Not-to-Exceed $350,000.00, RFP 24-42)
..Memorandum
Attached for your review and action is a resolution to approve a two (2) year construction contract with Watertap, Inc in the amount not-to-exceed $350,000.00 for the installation of water main line stops and insertable valves.

Each year Public Works encounters situations where sections of water mains must be isolated to replace valves, install fire hydrants or make emergency repairs. Installation of temporary line stops and valves enable this work to be performed with minimal interruption of water service. 

The request for proposals was advertised on the City's website and on the Michigan Intergovernmental Trade Network (MITN) website. One (1) proposal was received and publicly opened on July 26, 2024. A selection committee comprised of Public Services staff reviewed the proposal and determined that the proposal was the Best Value based on the criteria in ORD-21-41: 

* Qualifications, Experience, & Accountability (20%)
* Workplace Safety (20%)
* Workforce Development (20%)
* Social Equity & Sustainability (20%)
* Schedule of Pricing/Cost (20%)

Staff recommends that City Council approve a contract with Watertap, Inc. for this service. Watertap, Inc. complies with the City's Non-Discrimination, Conflict of Interest and Living Wage ordinances.

This contract was bid with the understanding that it could be extended for one (1) additional 2-year term at the mutual consent of the City and the Contractor with a one-time cost escalator of 3%. This Resolution would authorize the City Administrator to approve such an extension. 

Budget/Fiscal Impact:  Funding is available in the approved FY25 Water System Operation and Maintenance Budget and will be available in subsequent budgets if approved by council.

Watertap, Inc. complies with the City's Non-Discrimination and Living Wage Ordinances.

Reviewed by:       Sue F. McCormick, Interim Public Services Area Administrator
Approved by:       Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, Isolation of water mains is periodically needed to replace inoperable valves, install fire hydrants or perform emergency repairs;

Whereas, Installation of line stops and insertable valves enables this work to be performed with minimal interruption of water service;

Whereas. One (1) proposal from Watertap, Inc. was received by Purchasing on July 26, 2024;

Whereas, Watertap, Inc. is highly qualified to perform the work identified in RFP 24-42;

Whereas, The term of the proposed contract with Watertap, Inc. is for two years and up to $350,000.00, subject to the availability of funding; and

Whereas, Watertap Inc. complies with the City's Non-Discrimination, Conflict of Interest and Living Wage Ordinances;

matters.title: Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Spaans Babcock Inc. for the Purchase of Replacement Side Profiles on Screw Pumps #4 and #5 at the Water Resource Recovery Facility ($29,000.00)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Spaans Babcock Inc. for the Purchase of Replacement Side Profiles on Screw Pumps #4 and #5 at the Water Resource Recovery Facility ($29,000.00)
..Memorandum
Your approval is requested to authorize the purchase of replacement side profiles for screw pumps #4 and #5 at the Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) in the amount of $29,000.00.

The screw pumps are part of the WRRF's raw sewage lift station which is responsible for pumping incoming wastewater through the WRRF for treatment. These pumps are crucial in preventing wastewater from backing up in the sanitary sewer and causing a sanitary sewer overflow or into the basement of homes. 

On May 22, 2024, Spaans Babcock performed a condition assessment on the WRRFs screw pumps. In the report for screw pumps #4 and #5 they detailed the side profile steel showed significant delamination and broken supports due to the corrosive atmosphere. Replacement of the side profiles was suggested to extend the life of the pumps (estimated at 5-10 years of additional life) and prevent the failing side profiles from damaging other parts of the equipment. 

Spaans Babcock Inc. is the sole supplier of Spaans Babcock screw pumps and spare parts, this includes side profiles and deflectors. Screw pumps #4 and #5 were manufactured by Spaans Babcock Inc.

It is recommended that City Council approve a sole source purchase order for the replacement side profiles on screw pumps #4 and #5.
 
Budget/Fiscal Impact: Funds to finance this purchase are included in the approved FY25 WRRF Operations and Maintenance budget of the sewage disposal system. City Charter language requires sole source procurement over $25,000.00 receive City Council approval.
..Staff
Prepared by:     Nicholas Jaworski, Water Resource Recovery Services Asst. Manager 
                           Keith Sanders, Water Resource Recovery Services Manager 
Reviewed by:    Sue F. McCormick, Interim Public Services Area Administrator
Approved by:    Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas,  Screw pumps #4 and #5 are crucial to pumping incoming wastewater from the community into the City's WRRF preventing sanitary sewer overflows or basement backups;

Whereas,  Replacement of the side profiles will extend the life of the equipment by an estimated five to ten years and prevent possible damage from failure;

Whereas,  Spaans Babcock inc. is the sole supplier of parts for screw pumps #4 and #5; 

Whereas,  Spaans Babcock inc. complies with the City's conflict of interest and non-discrimination ordinances; and 

Whereas,  Funds to finance this purchase are included in the approved FY25 WRRF Operations and Maintenance budget of the sewage disposal system;

RESOLVED,  That City Council approves the sole source purchase order with Spaans Babcock Inc. for replacement side profiles on screw pumps #4 and #5 at the Water Resource Recovery Facility ($29,000.00); and 

RESOLVED,  That the City Administrator be authorized to take the necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.

matters.title: Resolution to Approve a Construction Contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. ($1,868,000.00, RFP 24-53) for the 2024 Valve Replacement Project
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Construction Contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. ($1,868,000.00, RFP 24-53) for the 2024 Valve Replacement Project
..Memorandum
Attached for your review and approval is a resolution to approve a construction contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc., in the amount of $1,868,000.00, for the 2024 Valve Replacement Project.

Currently there are a number of water main valves in the City's system that do not function properly and would not facilitate the isolation of segments of the water main system in case of failure. In cases when a water main shut down is required this may create additional inconvenience for the businesses and residents. This project includes replacement of 15 valves at multiple critical locations throughout the City. 

The construction of the project is scheduled to begin in February 2025 and continue through June 2025.

Engineering staff supervised the creation of plans and contract documents and bid the project through the City's Procurement Unit. On October 30, 2024, three proposals were received for this work. A selection committee comprised of Public Services staff reviewed the proposals and determined which bidder was the Best Value based on the criteria in ORD-21-41: 

* Qualifications, Experience, & Accountability (20%)
* Workplace Safety (20%)
* Workforce Development (20%)
* Social Equity & Sustainability (20%)
* Schedule of Pricing/Cost (20%)

After reviewing and scoring the proposals, staff ranked the responding firms in the following order:

1. E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc.
2. Fonson Company, Inc.
   3.	E & K Contractors

E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. (MacKenzie) received the highest score among the proposals reviewed by the selection committee. Therefore, staff recommends awarding the contract for this project to MacKenzie. MacKenzie complies with the City's Non-Discrimination and Living Wage ordinances.

Budget/Fiscal Impact:  The City of Ann Arbor Capital Improvements Plan (CIP) includes the 2024 Valve Replacement Projects (UT-WS-24-11). The total estimated project cost is $2,500,000. Funding for the project is included in the Water Supply System Fund Capital Budget.
..Staff
Prepared by:     Nicholas Hutchinson, P.E., City Engineer
Reviewed by:    Sue F. McCormick, Interim Public Services Area Administrator
Approved by:    Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, Many water main valves throughout the City are currently not functioning and would not be able to isolate parts of the water main system in the case of a break;

Whereas, Replacement valves must be installed for appropriate operation of the water system;

Whereas, The City of Ann Arbor received three proposals for this work on October 30, 2024 and E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. received the highest score among the proposals reviewed by the selection committee;

Whereas, It is now necessary to enter into a contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. for the performance of this work; and

Whereas, E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. complies with the City's Non-Discrimination, Conflict of Interest, and Living Wage ordinances;

RESOLVED, That City Council approve a construction contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. in the amount of $1,868,000.00 for the 2024 Valve Replacement Project (RFP 24-53);

RESOLVED, That a contract contingency amount of $200,000.00 be established within the project budget and that the City Administrator be authorized to approve additional change orders to the construction contract with E.T. MacKenzie Company, Inc. not to exceed $200,000.00 in order to satisfactorily complete this project;

RESOLVED, That the City make the following declaration for the purpose of complying with the reimbursement rules of Treasury Regulations 1.150-2 pursuant to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended: that the City reasonably expects to reimburse itself for expenditures for the costs of the Project with proceeds of Bonds;

RESOLVED, That the Mayor and City Clerk be authorized and directed to execute said contract after approval as to form by the City Attorney, and approval as to substance by the City Administrator; and

RESOLVED, That the City Administrator be authorized to take necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution, including issuing temporary and permanent Traffic Control Orders and night work authorizations as required for the construction of the project.

matters.title: Resolution to Approve Change Order No. 1 to the Contract with Huron Valley Electric, Inc. to Cover Additional Project Costs of $17,275.00 for the Fire Station 3 Emergency Generator, RFP #24-43 (Total Contract Amount: $82,275.00)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve Change Order No. 1 to the Contract with Huron Valley Electric, Inc. to Cover Additional Project Costs of $17,275.00 for the Fire Station 3 Emergency Generator, RFP #24-43 (Total Contract Amount: $82,275.00)
..Memorandum
Attached for your review and action is a resolution to approve Change Order No. 1 to the contract with Huron Valley Electric, Inc. for Fire Station 3 Emergency Generator, RFP #24-43 ($82,275.00)

In October 2024, Huron Valley Electric, Inc. was selected as the lowest responsible bidder with a cost of $65,000.00 based on specifications outlined in RFP #24-43. The project was to install an emergency generator at Fire Station 3. Fire Station 3 has never had an emergency generator and loses power more than any other fire station. This is due to the aging overhead infrastructure in the neighborhood that feeds it. The Office of Sustainability and Innovation was involved in significant research to determine the feasibility of battery or other alternative emergency power sources. None of these alternative power sources were determined to be cost feasible. 

When the project manager from Huron Valley Electric got into the work, it was discovered the power feeding into Station 3 is a very old, unique voltage called 120V/240V delta service. This voltage will not work with the new generator and does not meet the current electrical code. Huron Valley Electric has quoted an additional $17,275.00 to work with DTE to install a new transformer and resolve this voltage issue. 

As this Change Order No. 1 will place the total contract over the $75,000.00 threshold that requires City Council's approval, staff are seeking City Council's authorization to increase the contract amount for the Fire Station 3 Emergency Generator project from $65,000.00 to $82,275.00.  

Budget/Fiscal Impact: This project was an approved supplemental funding request for FY25, and this new amount is still within the budgeted funding amount. We are recommending a 5% project contingency of $4,113.75 to cover potential unanticipated items to be approved by the City Administrator if necessary.  
..Staff
Prepared by:		Chantel Jackson, Office Administrator - Fire
Reviewed by: 	Kim Buselmeier, Interim Chief Financial Officer
Reviewed by:		Mike Kennedy, Fire Chief
Approved by:		Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, Fire Station 3 has never had an emergency generator and loses power more than any other fire station; 

Whereas, Additional project work outside of the original scope of services was identified to address the power feeding into Station 3 for the new generator to work;

Whereas, This additional work exceeded the $75,000.00 Council approval limit;

Whereas, Change Order No. 1 with Huron Valley Electric, Inc. is recommended to be approved to complete this project; and 

Whereas, The new total contract amount is still within the budgeted funding;

RESOLVED, That City Council approve Change Order No. 1 to the Contract with Huron Valley Electric, Inc. to include the additional work required to install a new transformer and resolve this voltage issue, increasing the project by $17,275.00 and bringing the total amount of the contract to $82,275.00;

RESOLVED, That a contingency amount of $4,113.75 be established to fund any additional necessary services and that the City Administrator be authorized to approve change orders that do not exceed the contingency amount; 

RESOLVED, That all amounts approved herein are without regard to fiscal year;

RESOLVED, That the Mayor and City Clerk be authorized and directed to execute this Change Order after approval as to substance by the City Administrator and approval as to form by the City Attorney; and

RESOLVED, That the City Administrator be authorized to take the necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.

matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Revels Turf and Tractor LLC for the Purchase of a Greens Roller Manufactured by Agrimetal ($26,626.58) and Appropriate Funding ($28,696.00) (8 Votes Required)
..Memorandum
The attached resolution authorizes the purchase of one Greens Roller Model GR-660, manufactured by Agrimetal, for $26,626.58 for the Community Services Area, Parks, and Recreation Unit. This golf course equipment is used to maintain the city's two golf courses. During winter, it is stored indoors to prolong its life.
 
The new Agrimetal Greens Roller will replace the existing 2018 model (asset #6719) at Leslie Golf Course, which is now beyond its useful life as a front-line machine. Parks and Recreation have requested this machine due to its industry-leading 66" rolling width with a TriPlex roller design. This wider machine allows them to stay ahead of play and complete morning course setups efficiently. It remains towable by their vehicles and the three floating heads contour to the surface, eliminating rolling lines and ridges that smaller units cause, enhancing putting performance. The included trailer, with spring assist loading, is safer and easier for new staff to use.
 
Parks and Recreation will keep asset #6719 as a backup unit for the Huron Hills Golf Course and will pay the fleet the auction value to retain it.

Agrimetal is the sole manufacturer of a greens roller with the largest rolling width with a TriPlex roller design in the industry, model GR-660.

Revels Turf and Tractor LLC of Brighton, MI is the only dealer in the state that sells Agrimetal products.  

Revels Turf and Tractor LLC of Brighton MI, complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination ordinances.

Parks and Recreation is keeping the existing greens roller rather than selling it for its estimated auction value of $2,069.00 as a back-up roller.  

Budget/Fiscal Impact: The City continues to experience significant equipment price increases due to inflationary pressures and supply issues. matters.title: Resolution to Increase Sole Source Purchasing Authority with Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. (formerly SUEZ Treatment Solutions, Inc.) for Power Supply Units ($953,000.00 increase, total purchase value $1,728,552.60)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Increase Sole Source Purchasing Authority with Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. (formerly SUEZ Treatment Solutions, Inc.) for Power Supply Units ($953,000.00 increase, total purchase value $1,728,552.60)
..Memorandum
This memorandum and resolution requests approval to increase the purchasing authority with Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. (Veolia) (formerly SUEZ Treatment Solutions, Inc.) for furnishing power supply units (PSUs), ozone generator dielectrics and vessel internals for two (2) ozone generator trains required to provide primary disinfection at the Water Treatment Plant ($866,000.00).  

The Water Treatment Plant (WTP) provides reliable high-quality drinking water to approximately 140,000 customers. In 1996, the WTP completed a major improvements project that added ozone disinfection to be used as the WTP's primary disinfection step. Ozone is generated on-site via four (4) ozone generation equipment trains, each train consisting of power supply units, generator vessel dielectrics and internals, as well as various ancillary components. In 2022, a purchase order was issued to SUEZ (now Veolia) for two (2) of the PSUs that cost $775,552.60. These new units were commissioned in late 2023 and have been performing well.  This resolution increases the purchasing authority in order to purchase the other two (2) ozone PSUs. These remaining PSUs are original equipment from the 1996 installation and are nearing the end of their service life. Ensuring all four (4) ozone trains are available for operation is critical to maintain rated treatment capacity as regulated by EGLE. Completion of the Ozone system upgrades phase 2 is programmed into the CIP to proceed with several other improvement projects, specifically Plant 1 replacement.

Since the 2022 purchase order, SUEZ was acquired by Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions (Veolia). With this acquisition, Veolia maintains engineering and the production of materials and equipment compatible with the City's original equipment. Veolia provided a proposal to provide power supply units (PSUs), ozone generator dielectrics and vessel internals for the remaining two (2) ozone generator trains, spare parts as well as shop drawing submittals and site services. Their proposal took into consideration the recent replacement of Units 1 and 2 which minimizes repeat efforts for programming and will allow efficient integration of PSU 3 and 4.  

It is recommended to increase the Sole Source Purchasing Authority with Veolia (formerly SUEZ) $953,000.00, and that Veolia be awarded a purchase order for $866,000.00 for the ozone generation equipment needed to maintain the critical primary disinfection process of the water treatment plant.

The resolution recommends a contingency in the amount of $87,000.00 for changes to the purchase order with Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. to cover unforeseen conditions.


By utilizing Veolia equipment, these upgrades have the benefit of reusing portions of the existing equipment, avoiding the need to replace the entire ozone generator.  Components from other manufacturers are not compatible and would require entire system replacement. The proposal from Veolia is the most economical solution to restoring full operation of the primary disinfection system and improving long-term reliability.  

Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. complies with the City's Living Wage and Non-Discrimination Ordinances.

Budget/Fiscal Impact: Funds for this purchase are available from the approved FY25 Water Supply System Fund Capital Budget and will be available in the FY26 budget if so, approved by Council.  
..Staff
Prepared by:		Emily Schlanderer, Water Treatment Plant Engineer
Reviewed by:		Jordan Roberts, Public Services Area Administrator
Approved by:		Milton Dohoney, Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, The ozone disinfection system at the City's Water Treatment Plant is the primary disinfection process and critical in providing reliable and high-quality drinking water to approximately 140,000 customers;

Whereas; The replacement of the remaining two (2) ozone generator trains' power supply units (PSUs), dielectrics and ozone generator vessel internals will replace critical components of the ozone disinfection system that have failed and are no longer available or supported by the original equipment manufacturer;

Whereas, It is necessary to purchase the ozone disinfection components to ensure continuous operation of the primary disinfection system;

Whereas, Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. is uniquely qualified to provide the ozone generation equipment and programming because they are the sole authorized vendor of this equipment in our service area;

Whereas, Funding in the amount of $953,000.00 for the power supply units (PSUs), dielectrics and ozone generator vessel internals is partially available in the approved FY25 Water Supply System Fund Capital Budget and the remainder will be available in the FY26 budget if so, approved by Council; and

Whereas, Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. complies with the City's Living Wage and Non-Discrimination ordinances;

RESOLVED, That City Council accepts the quotation for the two (2) ozone generator trains' power supply units (PSUs), dielectrics and ozone generator vessel internals, and approves the issuance of a Purchase Order to Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. in the amount of $866,000.00;

RESOLVED, That City Council approves a contingency in the amount of $87,000.00 to the purchase order with Veolia Water Technologies - Treatment Solutions USA, Inc. and that the City Administrator be authorized to approve additional purchase order changes not to exceed $1,728,552.60 in order to satisfactorily complete this project; and 

RESOLVED, That the City Administrator be authorized to take the necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.

..Title
Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Waterworks Systems & Equipment Inc. for New Flocculation Drive Stuffing Boxes ($40,169.00)
..Memorandum
This memo and resolution requests approval of a Sole Source/Best Source purchase order with Waterworks Systems & Equipment Inc. for new flocculation drive stuffing boxes. 

The Water Treatment Services Unit (WTSU) uses the flocculation process as a key step in water clarification and lime softening. Flocculation is a mixing process that allows particles to aggregate and form larger particles which are then removed through settling. The flocculation equipment is operated using motorized drive assemblies with various components in both submerged and non-submerged environments separated by a concrete wall. Flocculation Basin No. 4 consists of four (4) motor drives, and each drive includes a stuffing box assembly that provides a watertight seal where the drive shaft passes through the wall. In recent years, repair and maintenance efforts have increased, resulting in extended equipment downtime and frequent leakage through the stuffing boxes resulting in wet floors and drainage issues. The stuffing boxes in Basin No. 4 have reached the end of their service life and require replacement.

Waterworks Systems & Equipment Inc. is the only vendor capable of providing retrofit components for the WTSU flocculation equipment. Therefore, Waterworks Systems & Equipment Inc. is the sole source for replacement stuffing boxes. This purchase order provides the owner-procured equipment for installation under City's Capital Improvements Plan Project UT-WS-26-16. The construction contract for this CIP project is expected to be executed in January 2026, and the long lead time would result in missing the WTP's shutdown opportunity for installation if not procured sooner.

It is recommended that City Council approve a Sole Source/Best Source Purchase Order for the procurement of four new flocculation drive stuffing boxes.  

Budget/Fiscal Impact: Funds to finance this purchase are included in the approved Water Supply System Capital Budget.

Charter language requires best source goods procurement over $25,000.00 receive City Council Approval.

Prepared by: Emily Schlanderer, Water Treatment Plant Engineer

Whereas, Waterworks Systems & Equipment Inc. is the sole source to provide the correct components;

..Memorandum
Your approval is requested to authorize the purchase of polymer from Solenis LLC for the City's Water Resource Recovery Facility (WRRF) at the unit price of $1.01 per pound, with an estimated annual quantity of 400,000 pounds and a total estimated cost of $404,000.00 for FY27.

The WRRF utilizes two gravity belt thickeners to thicken biosolids from the secondary (biological) treatment process and three centrifuges to dewater biosolids for disposal in a landfill. Biosolids must be conditioned with polymers to ensure proper functionality and optimal performance of both the gravity belt thickeners and the centrifuges, making the biosolids suitable for landfill disposal.

Plant staff worked with multiple vendors to test various polymers and determine which products best meet the performance needs of the WRRF's thickening and dewatering systems. After testing and establishing performance requirements, staff advertised for two specific polymers under Invitation to Bid (ITB) No. 4787: SNF Polydyne, Clarifloc CE-1540 polymer and Solenis LLC, Zetag 8846FS (US). Either polymer is suitable for use in both the gravity belt thickeners and the centrifuges. Pricing was requested for these two polymers under ITB No. 4787, with pricing firm for one year.

The following bids were received in response to ITB No. 4787:
* Polydyne, Inc.
o Clarifloc CE-1540 - $1.12/pound delivered
* Solenis LLC
o Zetag 8846FS (US) - $1.01/pound delivered
Staff reviewed the bids for compliance with ITB No. 4787 specifications and recommends awarding the purchase to Solenis LLC, the lowest responsible bidder, for FY27.

It is further recommended that the agreement be eligible for up to three annual renewals, with any price adjustments tied to the Producer Price Index for Basic Chemical Manufacturing (PPI Code 3251), subject to mutual agreement between the supplier and the City Administrator.

..Memorandum
Attached for your review and approval is a resolution authorizing an increase to the existing sole source purchase order with Source One Environmental, LLC for parts, supplies, and equipment necessary to perform sanitary and storm sewer pipe lining in FY27. 

Public Works uses PipePatch pipe lining equipment to perform small spot lining repairs to sanitary and storm sewer pipes. Source One Environmental, LLC is the sole source provider for PipePatch lining and rehabilitation equipment in the Southeastern Michigan Region.

Spot lining is a "trenchless" technology that enables pipe repair or maintenance without disturbing the surface above. During spot lining, a small section of new material is pulled into the existing pipe covering the area of the deficiency, creating a new pipe inside the existing one. The process is not only cost effective but eliminates the need for extensive excavation and lengthy traffic control measures, thereby minimizing disruption. 

Sole source goods procurement over $25,000.00 requires City Council Approval per City Charter.

matters.title: Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Brown Equipment Company for the Purchase of (3) Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper Attachments ($80,985.00)
matters.text:
..Title
Resolution to Approve a Sole Source Purchase Order with Brown Equipment Company for the Purchase of (3) Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper Attachments ($80,985.00) 
..Memorandum
The attached resolution requests the approval of a source purchase order with Brown Equipment Company for the purchase of three (3) Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper attachments.

As the City continues to expand its protected bike lane network, the Public Works Unit is responsible for maintaining a growing amount of specialized infrastructure, including winter snow and ice removal.  This increase in protected bike lane mileage has created additional operational demands and corresponding need for equipment that can maintain these facilities safely and efficiently.

Funding for additional maintenance equipment was included in the approved FY27 budget. The planned investment includes two (2) Bobcat units requested under a separate resolution and three (3) Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper attachments. Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper attachments are a sweeping broom and plow blade combination attachment that will mount to the proposed new Bobcat units and one existing Bobcat unit. The new equipment will provide Public Works with the additional capacity and specialized equipment needed to support the City's expanding bike lane network and maintain reliable winter service.  

Current equipment only allows for staff to use a broom or a plow requiring them to return to the Wheeler Center to change between the two attachments. The new Combi Snow Plow and Sweeper attachments will allow staff to plow an area and immediately follow with a broom, reducing travel time and increasing efficiency. Timan is the only manufacturer that offers a single attachment that can sweep and or plow snow.

Brown Equipment Company is the sole source provider for Timan Equipment in the State of Michigan. 

Brown Equipment Company complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination ordinances.

Budget/Fiscal Impact: Funding for the purchase of this equipment and corresponding increased operating and maintenance costs are included in approved FY27 Major Streets Fund budget. Maintenance costs will continue to rise with the expansion of the protected bike lane network.  Recent growth has necessitated this specialized equipment and planned expansion will likely require increased staffing in upcoming budget cycles.
..Staff
Prepared by:		Robert West, Public Works Assistant Manager
Reviewed by:		Paul Matthews, Public Works Manager
			Jordan Roberts, Public Services Area Administrator
Approved by:  	Milton Dohoney Jr., City Administrator
..Body
Whereas, The Public Works Unit needs to purchase attachments for Bobcat equipment used for protected bike lane winter maintenance; 

Whereas, The City continues to expand its protected bike lane network; 

Whereas, Timan Combi Snow Plow and Sweepers will allow staff to plow an area and immediately follow with a broom using one attachment, reducing travel time and increasing efficiency;

Whereas, Timan is the only manufacturer that offers a single attachment that can sweep and or plow snow;
 
Whereas, Brown Equipment Company is the sole source provider for Timan Equipment in the State of Michigan;

Whereas, Brown Equipment Company complies with the requirements of the City's Conflict of Interest and Non-Discrimination Ordinances; and 
Whereas, Funds for the purchase of the proposed Timan attachments and increased operating and maintenance costs are included in the approved FY27 Major Streets Fund budget;

RESOLVED, That the City Council approve the issuance of a purchase order to Brown Equipment Company for three (3) Timan Combi Snow Plow Sweeper attachments from Brown Equipment Company in the amount of $80,985.00;

RESOLVED, That funds for the purchase be available without regard to fiscal year; and

RESOLVED, That the City Administrator be authorized to take the necessary actions to implement this resolution.
